message:
docs(history): the rollback point named 0.2.109 is the document that broke the field

The backup guard did its job -- it refused to overwrite -- and the result is still
wrong in a way worth naming. manifest-backups/0.2.109 holds 1534 bytes, nine
artifacts, no GNLinkSetup.exe: the manifest that could not finish a swap. The
good one is under a timestamped name, and nothing says so. Anyone rolling back by
name restores the outage.

It is wider than the verifier found: manifest-backups/0.2.108 is also nine
artifacts with no Setup. Every backup with a bare version name holds a document
that cannot complete an update; the only usable rollback point is the timestamped
one.

So #507's "the original was preserved" is true and reads wrong. The guard
guarantees it does not overwrite. It has no idea which one is good.

Server files untouched -- unrelated to 0.2.110 and not urgent. On the task list
with a direction to decide after review.

Also recorded, because it happened three times this round: reporting a pass
without checking. A test detail that re-read a different moment than the wait it
reported on; a signature tamper that tampered with nothing and published a valid
release while claiming refusal; a dry run that skipped all ten artifacts and said
all ten matched. Same family as the root cause of this whole incident -- a suite
that stubbed the failing function and was approved as real verification. Green
does not mean something was checked. All three were in reporting lines, not in
the code: a summary has to describe the work it just did.
